notes: The authored legendary encounters: the lake trio (docs/mechanics/WATER_MAP.md section 5), the four bespoke concepts (docs/world-building/STRUCTURE_DECISIONS.md section 4, docs/story/ENCOUNTERS.md:392-395) and the wake of the sleeping Celebi (data/sapling_celebi.json, EXP-023). Every other legendary is Tier B: paste a structure into a fitting biome and gate it by badge count, and none of that is here.

A legendary is an ENTITY, so a re-export erases it and it is summoned over RCON by tools/reapply.py (step R14L), never by a pack: `spawnpokemonat` inside a function spawns nothing until a /reload (EXP-046 question 1). The pack does what functions can: the chamber's blocks, the gate, the keeper.
Ground is the canonical heightmap through tools/ground.py, rounded, never a world (CLAUDE.md's ground rule). Every mouth_y and portal_y in this file is measured, not authored.

The chambers are parametric, not a noise model: a stone envelope filled first, then the void carved out of it. That is what makes the seal provable offline (tools/legendaries_audit.py) instead of needing a dilation over a world.

Each record's `status` decides whether tools/legendaries.py emits it. `sited` is emitted; anything else is data only and the generator refuses to write its blocks (fail closed), so a blocked site cannot reach a world by accident.
period_why: the driver is one `execute positioned ... if entity @a[distance=..R]` line per emitted encounter, rescheduled every 20 ticks, so six encounters cost six command lines a second, not sixty a tick. The Celebi keeper's shape (tools/sapling_celebi.py), chosen because docs/mechanics/TOWN_TICK_BUDGET.md is counting the idle floor.

defaults.shell_margin_why: docs/mechanics/WATER_BUILD_PLAN.md 4.5 audit 1: at least 4 blocks of rock round every void, no void connecting to the water but the passage. Here it is guaranteed by construction: the envelope is filled solid first and extends shell_margin beyond every carved block in all six directions.
defaults.pool_depth_why: the flooded passage must meet the pool below the pool's surface: pool_depth must exceed bore - 1, so 4 with a bore of 3.
defaults.clearance_why: the envelope's top must stand shell_margin + clearance_blocks below the LOWEST heightmap ground over its own footprint, so no chamber roof thins under a slope and no chamber breaks a lake bed.
defaults.sleeve_flatness_why: the shaft's sleeve is filled to the lowest ground over its footprint, so it never raises the bed; the mouth may stand at most this far above that, which bounds the unsleeved lip of the hole.
defaults.light_why: docs/STATE.md, 'Places are lit as towns': lanterns, never light blocks.

level_caps.why: data/level_cap.json (the owner, 2026-09-28): a Pokemon strictly over the thrower's RCT level cap breaks free from EVERY ball, a Master Ball included. A legendary authored above the cap of its own badge gate is therefore uncatchable, which would make the encounter a wall rather than a reward.
level_caps.source: READ OUT 2026-09-29, and it is not a table. RCT computes the cap per player as max(initialLevelCap, min over the player's NEXT trainers of that trainer's team's highest level + relativeLevelCap) (LevelUtils at rctmod v0.19.0-beta, quoted in docs/research/notes/level-cap-catch-block.md), with initialLevelCap 20 and relativeLevelCap 0 (modpack/config/rctmod-server.toml). It therefore depends on the campaign's own RCT series data, and our gyms and Elite Four are NOT in that data yet (only the 13 Route 1-3 trainers and the 5 mansion Channelers are, docs/STATE.md). The by_badges table that stood here (3:40 4:46 5:52 6:58 7:64 8:70 champion:80) was invented and is gone.
level_caps.upper_bound_why: an UPPER BOUND, not the cap. After n badges the next trainer set contains gym n+1, whose team's highest level is data/trainers.json generation_contract gym_ace_levels[n] (20 25 30 35 40 45 50 55); after 8 badges it contains the Elite Four at 60. The cap is the MINIMUM over that set, so it is at most this and is lower whenever a weaker required trainer of the tier is still undefeated. A legendary above this bound is therefore certainly uncatchable; one below it still has to be checked in game. The champion's own cap is unknown: nothing authored comes after champion_blue (62), and what LevelUtils returns for an empty next set has not been read.
level_caps.above_the_bound_note: NOT FIXED HERE. Eight of the ten levels in this file are above the bound above, so data/level_cap.json makes them uncatchable as authored; each record's cap_at_gate still carries the invented table's number, which is why tools/legendaries_audit.py passes them. Re-levelling them is a balance decision (trainer-balance-designer) and it changes six emitted packs, so it is left to the owner. Only celebi_wake, the record this session owned, was brought under the bound (docs/mechanics/CELEBI_WAKE.md).
level_caps.above_the_bound_why: EMPTY as of 2026-09-29. The owner decided every legendary sits at the upper bound of the badge that gates its chamber. Lugia is the exception and is UNRESOLVED: its gate is champion_cleared and the champion's cap is unknown (nothing authored comes after champion_blue at 62, and what LevelUtils returns for an empty next set has not been read), so its level is untouched at 75 and the owner is handling it. NOTE the bound is an UPPER bound, not the cap: sitting exactly on it is catchable only when the player has cleared every other required trainer of that tier. Each one still has to be confirmed in game.
level_caps.champion_band_why: SETTLED 2026-10-02 (docs/mechanics/LEAGUE_LEVEL_CAP.md): after the Champion the player's Kanto series has no next trainer, and rctmod v0.19.0-beta LevelUtils returns maxLevel() = 100 for an empty next set; completing a series never resets it. So the champion band is 100, not the 65 invented on 2026-09-30. tools/legendaries_audit.py rct_caps derives every band from data/trainers.json and the RCT config and checks each record's level and cap_at_gate against it.

spawn_free_zones_note: Every emitted encounter declares a `spawn_free_zone`: the chamber footprint snapped out to the 8-block grid the route boxes share. They are NOT written into data/spawn_suppression.json by this file's author, because that file was in flight in another session on 2026-09-29; whoever merges them must also accept that a spawn-free zone is a 2-D column, so a grotto's zone also silences the lake water directly above it (about 40 by 40 blocks of a lake that is 300+ across). tools/legendaries_audit.py checks the boxes are grid-snapped and cover their chamber.

encounters.blocked_why: NOT the water export any more, and not a siting computation. Three things were measured on 2026-09-29, on the canonical heightmap (which now IS the applied water export, sha d1bc68d3..., docs/STATE.md 'Canonical heightmap'), and each is fatal on its own. (1) THE AXIS IS OFF THE MAP. data/regions.json marine_regions[...].features.trench_axis runs (9000, 5200) -> (8600, 6200) -> (8200, 7400) -> (7400, 8400) -> (6200, 8900). The heightmap is 8192 x 8192 at origin (0, 0), so EVERY ONE of those five points is outside it: tools/ground.py raises IndexError at all five. The world border ring reaches 8703, but the ground under the outer margin is not in the heightmap the ground rule reads. (2) A TRENCH IS NOT A HEIGHTMAP FEATURE. docs/world-building/OCEAN.md puts the shrine at y-30 to y-40; the canonical heightmap's global minimum is y10.1. A floor below y10 cannot be expressed in it at all, so no export, past or future, can produce this trench: it has to be CARVED as blocks below the seabed, like a sealed chamber, not sited on a surface. (3) THE SEABED THERE IS NOT DEEP. Sampled just inside the map on the axis's own line: (8100, 7400) y49, (8000, 7800) y53, (7400, 8100) y45, (8100, 8100) y26. That is 10-40 blocks of water under sea level 62, not an abyss. So the trench is an unbuilt design, not a place, and building it is a world-design job (a spiral descent, three sealed air pockets, a flooded shrine with three door locks) that this generator's parametric grotto cannot express. It is also gated on content that does not exist: `requires_keys` names three shipwreck coves in three marine regions and none of them is sited in data/.

open_questions: Shared or per player? An entity's NBT is world state, so a qualified player who opens a grotto's inner door opens it for everyone standing in the chamber, and the first catch takes the encounter for the whole server. docs/mechanics/WATER_MAP.md decision 1 leaves this open for the trio and ENCOUNTERS.md:397 leaves it open for Lugia. Nothing here decides it; the build is shared, and per player would need the scene runtime's per-player actors (EXP-034, which needs a second account).

A woken legendary can be killed. Cobblemon's PokemonEntity ignores Invulnerable and a sword killed the Celebi in three hits (EXP-023). While a chamber is shut the barrier door or the stone plug is the protection; once open, the legendary is as killable as any placed Pokemon. The re-application restores it, but within a session it is gone and the keeper cannot summon it back (functions cannot run Cobblemon's spawn command, EXP-046). No answer is proposed here.

The level cap. RCT computes it per player from the series data and our gyms are not in that data yet; level_caps.upper_bound_by_badges bounds it from the authored ladder, and eight of the ten levels here are above that bound (level_caps.above_the_bound). A legendary above its gate's cap cannot be caught at all.
The badge gates of the four bespoke encounters are this file's proposals. Only the trio's (3, 5, 7) and Lugia's (Dive and champion_cleared) are the owner's.

Celebi's wake item. The pack emits minecraft:clock as a proposal and nothing in the campaign teaches a wake item; docs/story/EARLY_ROUTE_BUILD_HANDOFF.md forbids a Route 1 NPC naming one, so it has to be taught after gym 8.

A woken Celebi stays on its branch about 20 blocks above the clearing (NoAI and NoGravity are kept), so the player must climb to it to battle or throw a ball. Whether it should instead descend is a design call and a data change.
